verification_clause_overlap.leakage_mechanism: OpenSec-Triage generates alerts by pairing parameterized scenario bodies with fixed pools of ~14-15 syntactic verification/evidence clauses per class (for A, B, C, F, G). While asset names, principals, and timestamps are randomized, 100% (700/700) of validation records contain identical trailing verification clauses that uniquely correlate with ground-truth labels in the training corpus.

non_conservative_details.classification: Non-conservative downgrade from security threat to operational fault

latency_audit.explanation: The apparent 1,830.6 ms/sample vs 393.5 ms/sample latency discrepancy was caused by an un-warmed initial run and JIT compilation / initial PyTorch CUDA context initialization delay during the first 100 samples of evaluate_pilot_val.py (which took 920.5s for 100 samples = ~9.2s/sample). Over the subsequent 600 samples (200 to 700), the pilot run completed in 360.9s, yielding ~601.5 ms/sample. Controlled warm single-call benchmarking confirms base model latency is 441.5 ms/call and pilot adapter latency is 575.0 ms/call (LoRA overhead is ~133.5 ms/call, not 1,437 ms).

verdict_justification: While there are 0 exact duplicates and only 4.4% near-duplicates at Jaccard >= 0.80, 100% of validation records share identical trailing verification clauses with the training set. OpenSec-Triage relies on synthetic template grammars where ~14 canonical verification clauses per class act as near-deterministic labels. Consequently, the 97.00% validation accuracy reflects successful template-pattern fitting rather than proven generalized reasoning on unseen telemetry.

recommended_independent_evaluation.dataset_candidate: Boss of the SOC (BOTS) v1-v3 / Splunk Security Content or Certified CIC-IDS/CSE-CIC-IDS2018 Incident Triage Scenarios
recommended_independent_evaluation.requirements: Real-world or human-authored SOC decision logs with diverse grammatical formulations and independent ground-truth adjudication.
